findings.title: Broken cleanup registration uses literal 'alias' instead of actual IDP alias
findings.body: In the new test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, each cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)`. The literal string "alias" does not match any identity provider actually created in the test (which uses aliases like "idp-alias-0" through "idp-alias-19"). `identityProviders().get("alias")` therefore returns null, and the bound method reference `null::remove` will throw a NullPointerException when the cleanup is invoked, or the cleanup will silently be a no-op. The cleanup should use the actual alias (e.g., `"idp-alias-" + i`). This is copied from the existing `testCacheIDPByOrg` test (line 303) but the new test propagates the bug to 20 more IDPs, increasing the risk of test pollution and teardown failures across the suite.

findings.title: Inconsistent model wrapping causes login predicate to evaluate differently on original vs updated
findings.body: In `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(IdentityProviderModel original, IdentityProviderModel updated)`, `original` comes from `getById(model.getInternalId())` and is therefore wrapped in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (the anonymous subclass defined at line 434 that overrides `isEnabled()` to also check the linked organization's enabled status). The `updated` parameter, however, is the raw `model` passed to `update()` and is NOT wrapped. `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` uses `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled`, which is polymorphic: on `original` it dispatches to the overridden (organization-aware) `isEnabled()`, but on `updated` it dispatches to the raw `isEnabled()`. The predicate therefore returns different values for the same logical IDP depending on which side of the comparison is being evaluated, leading to inconsistent invalidation decisions. For example, if an IDP is linked to a currently disabled organization, `test(original)` returns false but `test(updated)` returns true, causing both early-return guards to fail and triggering a wasteful cache invalidation. In race conditions where the organization is enabled at `getById` time but disabled by the time the predicate runs (or vice versa), the asymmetry can also produce missed invalidations, leaving stale entries in the login cache. The fix is to wrap it before evaluation (e.g., `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(updated)`), or to use a non-polymorphic raw-enabled check consistently inside the invalidation helpers.
